pat.law: Moens-Korteweg / Bramwell-Hill: PWV ~ sqrt(Eh/2rho R), and stiffer vessel at higher BP => faster wave => SHORTER arrival time. Longer PAT must predict LOWER BP.

rise.law: Systolic upstroke time falls as ejection meets a stiffer, higher-pressure arterial tree. Longer rise => LOWER BP.

aix.law: Augmentation index: faster PWV returns the reflected wave into systole, raising late systolic pressure. Higher AIx => HIGHER BP.

hr.law: Rate-pressure coupling under sympathetic drive (BP = CO x SVR, CO = HR x SV). Weak/ambiguous: SV falls as HR rises.

decay.law: Diastolic decay ~ RC windkessel time constant; depends on both compliance and resistance, so the BP sign is not fixed.

amp.law: NEGATIVE CONTROL: per-segment amplitude normalization removes scale, so a faithful model must be INSENSITIVE to gain.
